memory_update.text: Keep Murata/MRAAY as the primary reference anchor for AI-server high-end MLCCs; evidence is strong but it is not an underfollowed discovery candidate.
Keep TDK/TTDKY as a second reference anchor because official TDK material explicitly maps MLCC products to data-center AI-server power systems.

Promote Vishay/VSH to Layer 2 verification as a mid-cap underfollowed passive-component candidate, but require proof of AI-server/data-center socket exposure rather than generic capacitor/inductor exposure.
Promote Knowles/KN as an underfollowed specialty-capacitor hypothesis; its MLCC capability is factual, but AI-server board-level bottleneck relevance is not yet proven.

US-listed access to the most relevant Asian MLCC suppliers is imperfect: several leaders are OTC ADRs or foreign ordinary listings, and Samsung Electro-Mechanics, Taiyo Yuden, Yageo/KEMET, and Kyocera AVX require a separate listing/liquidity and evidence pass.

Layer 2 should distinguish GPU-adjacent decoupling MLCCs from PSU/IBC capacitors, inductors, current-sense resistors, and distributor inventory because scarcity and margins may differ sharply by socket.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the high-end AI-server MLCC and board-level passive-component node. The cleanest reference anchors are Murata and TDK via US OTC ADRs because both have explicit AI/data-center MLCC or server-capacitor evidence. The underfollowed lane is weaker but investable for later research: Vishay has broad capacitors, MLCCs, low-ESR/high-current passive products and a mid-cap market-cap profile; Knowles has specialty MLCC and high-reliability capacitor exposure but AI-server linkage remains a hypothesis requiring customer and product-fit verification.
